_comment: keep-raw decisions for iznik-spatial-go, per plan section 7.4/7.5
(plans/database-migration-evaluation-2026-07.md).
This service does not import gorm.io/gorm (confirmed against go.mod and by
grepping the tree) - it talks to MySQL and to its own local SQLite index
purely via database/sql. Scoping this service found no wave 1-3 mechanical
opportunity large enough to justify adding a GORM dependency and the
4-layer parity harness for it, so every site here is keep-raw rather than
raw/in-progress. See tools/orm-migration/README.md and the scoping report
in the team's session history for the full reasoning.
Two categories are deliberately kept distinct, per plan 7.4 - a hard-site
list that blurs 'irrelevant to the migration' with 'a real MySQL statement
that must be ported' tells Phase 4 the wrong thing:
- 'Not applicable' sites do not touch the Percona/MySQL cluster this
migration is about at all (the local SQLite spatial index in index.go),
or are not part of the built service (compare.go, //go:build ignore).
These need NO Phase 4 work and should not appear in that estimate.
- Real sites are genuine MySQL statements against the migrated database
that stay raw for now, each with an honest per-dialect porting note -
what the statement becomes on PostgreSQL, not just 'this one is hard'.
Rules match on file plus optional function, exactly as in the main
tools/orm-migration/keep-raw.json. This file is independent of that one -
it does not share IDs or state with it.

rules.reason: Operates on this service's own local, on-disk SQLite R-tree spatial index (the items/items_rtree tables created by CreateIndex/initSchema/OpenIndex), not the shared Percona/MySQL cluster. Directly analogous to the existing iznik-server-go/userdump/sqlite.go keep-raw precedent, which the main manifest already excludes for the identical reason.
rules.porting: Not applicable: this SQLite index is local runtime state, rebuilt from the real MySQL/Postgres source tables by the Load/ApplyDelta functions elsewhere in this package. It is unaffected by the MySQL-to-PostgreSQL migration and should not be counted in the Phase 4 estimate.

rules.reason: Standalone comparison utility guarded by "//go:build ignore"; not compiled into the service binary, run manually via `go build -o compare compare.go`. It already connects to both MySQL and a separate PostgreSQL comparison host directly (its hardcoded PostgreSQL credential was removed in PR #1231 after being found during this scoping pass; that credential needs rotating regardless of anything in this manifest).
rules.porting: Not applicable for Phase 4: this is a one-off dev tool, not a migration target. If it is kept after the cutover it would need MySQL's ORDER BY RAND() changed to PostgreSQL's ORDER BY RANDOM(); ST_X/ST_Y/ST_Centroid are already dialect-portable, PostGIS uses the same names.

rules.reason: Loads MySQL-only ST_AsWKB(polyindex) group-boundary geometry for the local spatial index; the same spatial-extraction shape plan 7.5 already keeps raw in iznik-server-go (message/bounds.go), and a rewrite bug here would silently corrupt every group-boundary lookup this service serves.
rules.porting: PostGIS: ST_AsWKB is the identical function name and output (WKB bytes). Backtick-quoted `groups` -> unquoted or double-quoted "groups" (it is not a Postgres reserved word). WHERE publish=1 AND listable=1 AND polyindex IS NOT NULL is unchanged, ANSI SQL.

rules.reason: Extracts job geometry as WKB for the local spatial index; core to the service's purpose, high blast radius if silently wrong.
rules.porting: PostGIS: ST_AsWKB is unchanged. COALESCE and comparison operators are unchanged - no MySQL-only syntax beyond the one spatial function.

rules.reason: Trivial single-table COUNT with a plain WHERE clause; a legitimate mechanical ORM candidate on its own merits, but converting one isolated site is not worth adding a GORM dependency to a service that has none today. Deferred alongside the rest of this service's inventory rather than converted piecemeal.
rules.porting: No change required for PostgreSQL: ANSI SELECT/COUNT/WHERE, no MySQL-only syntax.
rules.category: Mechanical, deferred (no GORM in this service)

rules.reason: Trivial single-table MAX(); same deferral reason as liveCount above - mechanical but not worth new infrastructure for a single site.
rules.porting: MySQL CAST(x AS CHAR) -> PostgreSQL CAST(x AS TEXT) (or x::text). MAX() is unchanged.
rules.category: Mechanical, deferred (no GORM in this service)

rules.reason: Trivial single-table SELECT with a plain WHERE clause; same deferral reason as the other wave-1 sites in this service.
rules.porting: No change required for PostgreSQL: ANSI SELECT/WHERE, no MySQL-only syntax.
rules.category: Mechanical, deferred (no GORM in this service)

rules.reason: Trivial single-table SELECT with no predicate at all; same deferral reason as the other wave-1 sites in this service.
rules.porting: No change required for PostgreSQL: ANSI SELECT, no MySQL-only syntax.
rules.category: Mechanical, deferred (no GORM in this service)

rules.reason: Extracts point geometry (ST_X/ST_Y) plus a CASE expression for the local spatial index; same high-blast-radius spatial-extraction shape as dataset_groups.go Load.
rules.porting: PostGIS: ST_X/ST_Y are the identical function names and semantics on a geometry column. CASE WHEN...END and the LEFT JOIN are unchanged, ANSI SQL.

rules.reason: Extracts point geometry (ST_X/ST_Y) for the local spatial index; same spatial-extraction shape as dataset_messages.go ApplyDelta.
rules.porting: PostGIS: ST_X/ST_Y are unchanged. COALESCE and comparison operators are unchanged, no other MySQL-only syntax.
